gold:
1) A resolved category chain must never outlive the run that resolved it. No lru_cache on catalog.categories.resolve_chain, no module level dict of chains, nothing process wide: the chain a run resolves dies with that run, and the rule binds every module in the service, not just the enrichment job.
2) The taxonomy team's nightly rebalancer edits category records in place between our runs. It renames nodes and re-parents leaves on the live taxonomy, so a chain held over from an earlier run is quietly describing a category that has since moved.
3) Last quarter a memoizing resolver kept serving chains across runs and we shipped stale category alias data to the storefront, so live product pages carried category paths that had already been renamed.
4) Batching, not caching. Build a per-run index that resolves each distinct category exactly once inside the run and throw it away when the run ends; enrich_all, the weekly check job and the cli paths command each build their own.

The standing rule out of last quarter's postmortem is that a resolved category chain never outlives the run that resolved it, so nothing in this service may memoize resolve results at module level or process wide, and an lru_cache on catalog.categories.resolve_chain is specifically out. The reason is the taxonomy team's nightly rebalancer, which edits category records in place between our runs, renaming nodes and re-parenting leaves under us; a chain we held from an earlier run is pointing at a category that has since moved, and nothing in our code notices. That is not hypothetical. Last quarter a memoized resolver held chains across runs and we shipped stale alias data to the storefront, which is the incident the rule came out of. Making the tooling cheaper is still fair game, but the sanctioned way is batching rather than caching: resolve each distinct category exactly once inside a run, through an index built when the run starts and thrown away when it ends.

Short version: never cache resolved chains across runs, batch inside a run instead. The rebalancer moves categories under us, and caching them cost us a storefront incident last quarter.

In detail:

- The rule. A resolved category chain must not survive the run that resolved it. No process wide or module level memo of resolve results, no lru_cache on the resolver. Every module here is bound by it, not only catalog/enrich.py.
- Why it exists. The taxonomy team runs a nightly rebalance that edits category records in place between our runs, renaming categories and re-parenting them, so anything cached from a previous run is stale the moment that batch lands.
- Last quarter. A memoizing resolver served chains across runs and we shipped stale category alias data to the storefront; the listings carried aliases that had already been renamed before anyone caught it.
- The sanctioned speedup. Batch within the run: a per-run index that resolves each distinct category exactly once and is discarded when the run ends. That is how enrich_all, the weekly check job and the cli paths command are meant to get cheap.

Nothing in this repository documents a caching rule, so what follows is what the code shows plus my own reading of it.

Three call sites resolve category chains through catalog/categories.py: catalog/enrich.py per record, catalog/checks.py per record, and the cli paths command per record. All three go through taxonomy_api.resolve on every lookup, so there is no memoization at all today, and no comment says whether that is deliberate or just unoptimized.

If I had to justify it, the argument would be that the taxonomy is owned by another team and can change without warning, so re-reading it is the safe default. I have no evidence of a production incident last quarter; there is no history in the checkout to consult and I would rather not invent one.

On cost, the change I would propose is a per-run index: resolve the distinct cat_ids once at the start of each run, 32 of them against 1451 products, and reuse those chains for the rest of the run.
